positions.name: SprintRetroDeliveryEvidence
positions.frame: What does the sprint retrospective offer as evidence that the decision-capture feature shipped and worked?
positions.why: The three assertions build one evidentiary case in sequence: a completed delivery ('We shipped the async decision widget'), a quantified measure of that delivery's pace ('23 points, highest this quarter'), and a causal account of what drove the pace ('the Zephyr integration was the key unlock'). Directional reads show a register shift across the set — src-1 sits in communal-sharing/activated-positive framing ('we shipped', the team acting together) while src-2 and src-3 pivot into technical, market-pricing framing (points, integration-as-lever) — but all three share past/realis/concrete temporal grounding and 'claim'-level conviction, and together they read as the retro's single justification narrative: delivered, measured, explained. The tension between the communal announcement and the metric/causal framing is held, not resolved — it is how the retro moves from 'we did it' to 'here is why it counted'.
